name: Self-Directed Dimension of Singletons
proof: At $n=1$, Player A can label the whole chosen set correctly before any Player B move, giving payoff zero; leaving a point would allow B to assign the wrong label and obtain payoff $-1$. For $n\ge2$, on a one-coordinate set both labels are realized. A leaves it to B and guarantees one move, so the dimension is at least one. For any $S$, B can assign label one at its first available move. If this is unrealizable, the payoff is $-1$. Otherwise that positive label identifies a unique singleton. A must then finish all remaining labels before another B move, since B could assign a label contradicting that singleton. Hence B can keep the payoff at most one. The dimension is therefore one, agreeing with the general self-directed mistake-bound identity.
references: \cite{devulapalli2024selfdirected}, Section 3 labelling game; direct singleton calculation
